en: "Jin-zhi! Jin-zhi!
The Emperor, hearing these words, had tears streaming down his face.
After a long while, he said to the Monk, "In my small kingdom, there is absolutely nothing by way of offerings. Yet for several years, you have resided within its midst."
I have no intention of showing you disrespect.
Although I am a sovereign ruling over this world,
I offer my constant thanks for your Eminence’s visit to this small kingdom.
"I humbly pray that the Venerable Master will remain out of compassion for another three or five days,
so that I may know whether I have attained it or not. Master Yuan said,
"As for the meaning of Nirvana, it is fundamentally free from攀緣 (pán yuán— clinging to objects)."
If there is any object of attachment, it all belongs to delusive thought.
I pray that Your Majesty will not harbor sorrow.
This poor monk has a vow to return to the mountains.
When the Emperor saw him,
Master Yuan’s words were so earnest that it was as if his sincere feelings could not be contained.
An imperial decree was issued to inform the Six Palaces in advance to secretly prepare for the funeral procession.
At that time, the Emperor, filled with longing and affection, sent forth high ministers from throughout the realm to see him off together.
As Master Yuan ascended the road, he departed from the imperial palace and took leave of the Dragon Tower.
Gazing at Mount Tai, the road is far;
beholding the rivers and lakes, one wanders with ease.
On this day, Master Yuan was able to traverse the long journey and reach his destination.
He then secretly manifested supernatural powers.
As Master Huiyuan emerged from Chang’an, clouds rose from his feet;
like a strong man extending his arm, they reached Mount Lu in a mere instant.
Master Yuan also did not return to his former temple;
rather, having traveled ten *li* away,
he temporarily constructed a thatched hut atop a steep ridge.
There, he sat cross-legged and immediately sought out the old scroll once more;
as he raised his voice again to recite the sutra, several more months passed by in the blink of an eye.
Master Yuǎn suddenly gazed toward the high plateau and called out, "Come up here!
That realm was of steep peaks where cranes cried in the ravines and dragons roared at their bases.
In the hundreds of valleys and thousands of peaks, flowers bloom as a matter of course;
upon the level ground flow long-running waters,
and in the gardens bloom flowers that never decay.
This is the place where the Tathāgata practiced his cultivation.
Thereupon, the Venerable Yuanjing sat upright and entered into samādhi.

With a pure mind and a tranquil consciousness, he contemplated the Buddha-way; reflecting that this floating life is not long-lasting and that the mundane world is incapable of sustaining him, he took his own sovereign mind-king and fashioned a Dharma-vessel, taking refuge in the higher realms.
Master Yuan Gong did not use the materials for building the boat;
they were all ordinary worldly supplies and required no special kinds whatsoever.
Holding oneself by means of the untainted (*anāsrava*),
one takes the Mahāyāna as the tethering rope and bodhicitta and prajñā as the enclosure railing.
The Vajrapāṇi Guhyapada has already [bestowed this] upon □□□.
Recorded by Zhang Changji in the fifth year of the Kaiyuan era.
